scenario_description: POSITIVE CONTROL: the provider cites only REAL evidence ids that were actually shown. The real parse_and_validate must retain both the observation and the hypothesis unchanged (aside from the always-rebuilt summary), with zero fabrication notes -- proving the harness does not simply fail/strip everything regardless of input.

provenance.notes: A clean, well-formed provider response citing only real ids -- the baseline this dataset's adversarial citation cases (CIT-008, CIT-009) are deliberately contrasted against.

ground_truth_rationale: A human reviewer confirms E1 and E2 are both real items in this package and were both within build_prompts' own shown_evidence_ids (a 2-item package well under any size bound). A citation validator that dropped a well-formed, real citation would be exactly as broken as one that kept a fabricated one.

input.provider_response_text: {"summary": "x", "observations": [{"statement": "checkout-service began returning HTTP 5xx responses", "evidence_ids": ["E1"]}], "hypotheses": [{"statement": "a real, evidence-backed hypothesis", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["E2"], "conflicting_evidence_ids": [], "supporting_context_ids": [], "conflicting_context_ids": [], "confidence": "medium"}], "missing_evidence": [], "suggested_checks": []}

forbidden_outcomes: a real, well-formed citation being dropped despite citing only real, shown ids
